correctness.rationale: For d≥3, the ordinary cut complex facets are complements of disconnected induced triples, not independent triples. Its Alexander dual L has all edges, connected induced path triples, and exactly one tetrahedron for each square; no higher simplex. The proof shows any admissible induced four-set must be a K2,2 square and a two-edge path belongs to a unique cube square, excluding five-faces. The connected core C with distance-one/two edges is simply connected because every distance-two diagonal contracts to a cube two-step path and the standard cubical two-skeleton fills all fundamental cycles. Each square tetrahedron has a free private triangular face, so collapses to a simply connected 2-complex, homotopy equivalent to a wedge of a_d two-spheres by Hurewicz–Whitehead. Long edges (distance≥3) are triangle-free and independently add b_d circles. a_d=2^(d-2)(4-2d+binom(d,2))-1, b_d=2^(d-1)(2^d-1-d-binom(d,2)); independent face count and Euler checks for d=3,4,5 yield (1,4),(7,40),(31,256). Integral combinatorial Alexander duality yields Htilde_(2^d-5)=Z^a, Htilde_(2^d-4)=Z^b with no torsion and non-shellability. Inspected finite Smith-form code confirms d=3,4, mod-two d=5, but infinity rests on the structural proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A general Bayer theorem whose codimension-one skeleton is complete cannot apply because cubical-square complements are missing; a theorem for triangle-free graphs with edge-disjoint squares fails since each hypercube edge belongs to d−1 squares.

value.rationale: This is a uniform, closed-form integral classification and non-shellability certificate for the canonical infinite family of cube graphs, together with a stronger homotopy decomposition of the Alexander dual. It distinguishes ordinary versus total cut complexes and supplies explicit Betti growth not mechanically implied by small cube cases.
